sources.citation: Y. Chang et al., Journal of Crystal Growth 277, 78-84 (2005)
sources.title: Composition and thickness distribution of HgCdTe molecular beam epitaxy wafers by infrared microscope mapping

specimens.reported_structure: higher Cd composition and lower thickness in small corner regions
large edge-to-center composition and thickness gradients

measurement.instrument: Thermo Nicolet Centaurus infrared microscope coupled to a Thermo Nicolet 870 FTIR
measurement.spatial_kernel_statement: The 100 um aperture is a stated integration footprint, not a measured optical PSF.
measurement.fit_method: interference-matrix transmission model with Levenberg-Marquardt and simulated annealing

scientific_constraints: Reported wafer-map standard deviations combine deterministic edge or corner drift with any stochastic local variation.
The figures demonstrate nonstationarity and anticorrelation between Cd composition and HgCdTe thickness at wafer scale.
Stage positioning precision is not equivalent to spatial resolution.
The numerical fitting convergence thresholds are not measurement uncertainties.
The map cannot identify 10-500 nm covariance because the stated aperture is 100 um and the sampling pitch is not explicitly reported.

feasible_outputs: coarse digitization of wafer-scale composition and thickness trends
bounded comparison of center versus edge nonuniformity

sources.citation: F. X. Zha et al., Applied Physics Letters 101, 141604 (2012)
sources.title: Implication of exotic topography depths of surface nanopits in scanning tunneling microscopy of HgCdTe

surface_and_instrument.surface_preparation: Br2/methanol etch followed by pure methanol rinse
calibration_checks: single-wall carbon nanotube height on gold

scientific_constraints: Flat-region spectra show a roughly 0.40 eV zero-current plateau, larger than the reported 0.27 eV bulk gap, and are interpreted as tip-induced band bending.
Pit spectra A-C have finite in-gap slopes attributed to high densities of gap states; pit D shows a plateau approximately equal to the reported gap.
Bias-polarity changes can alter apparent pit depth by 20-30 nm without a geometric change.
STM topography over HgCdTe cannot be treated as a geometric or composition field without bias-polarity and transport controls.
No measurement temperature, modulation amplitude, energy calibration uncertainty, or measured energy-resolution kernel is reported.

feasible_outputs: digitization of apparent pit-depth and bias-polarity line profiles
digitization of flat-region and pit I-V curves for nuisance-model bounds
lower-bound demonstration of TIBB and defect-state contamination
prohibited_outputs: geometric pit-depth field from a single bias

useful_prior_constraints: coarse MBE wafer nonuniformity and deterministic spatial drift
HgCdTe-specific TIBB, transport-limited tunneling, pit gap states, and non-geometric topography artifacts

stop_rules: Do not combine the two papers into one specimen or exchangeable population.
Do not treat Chang wafer-map standard deviation as nanoscale random-mass variance.
Do not treat the 100 um aperture as a measured PSF.
Do not treat Zha STM topography as a geometric or composition map.
Do not infer a spectroscopy kernel from nominal bias or the reported bulk gap.
Do not reactivate R05 from figure-derived literature constraints.
